# Adjudication Task — Chapter 694

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃694화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|달마저 가려진 깊은 밤.
  6|
  7|짙은 어둠에 잠겨 있던 산골짜기에, 희미한 불꽃이 피어오르기 시작했다.
  8|
  9|하나, 둘, 셋. 그리고 이내 수백으로 불어난 횃불과 함께 세상이 흔들린다.
 10|
 11|드드드득!
 12|
 13|지면을 통해 전해지는 떨림. 바람에 휘청이는 횃불 아래에는 크고 작은 그림자와 거친 숨결이 쉼 없이 뿜어졌다.
 14|
 15|크르릉.
 16|
 17|후우. 후.
 18|
 19|군세(軍勢).
 20|
 21|그것은 수많은 인간과 짐승이 뒤섞인 하나의 군세였다.
 22|
 23|검과 창, 활로 무장한 남만의 전사들은 안장 위에 앉아 쉴 새 없이 어둠 너머를 눈으로 더듬고 있었고, 날카로운 이빨과 발톱을 지닌 맹수들은 계속 달려 나갔다.
 24|
 25|그 숫자가 물경 삼천.
 26|
 27|그리고 오직 한 사람의 명령에 따라, 정오 무렵 외궁을 벗어난 그들의 목적지는 처음부터 정해져 있었다.
 28|
 29|‘애뇌산(哀牢山).’
 30|
 31|선두에서 내달리던 호위장의 머릿속에 떠오른 세 글자. 그와 동시에 그의 등 뒤에서 누군가의 외침이 터져 나왔다.
 32|
 33|“보입니다!”
 34|
 35|과연 그 말대로였다.
 36|
 37|호위장은 물론 모두가 볼 수 있었다. 삼천에 달하는 군세가 지닌 횃불과는 비교도 되지 않는 강렬하고, 거대한 화마(火魔)가 일렁이는 모습을.
 38|
 39|우둑, 콰아아아!
 40|
 41|나이를 가늠할 수 없는 거목이 줄지어 쓰러지고, 닿는 모든 것을 탐욕스럽게 집어삼킨 불길이 더욱더 몸집을 부풀린다.
 42|
 43|백 년 전에도 없었고, 어쩌면 백 년 뒤에도 없을 대화재(大火災)을 지켜보는 전사들의 입술 사이로 침음성이 흘러나왔다.
 44|
 45|“이, 이럴 수가.”
 46|
 47|“그게. 그게 사실이었다니…….”
 48|
 49|다른 사람의 입을 통해 전해 듣는 것과 직접 눈으로 확인하는 것은 다르다.
 50|
 51|불길에 휩싸인 애뇌산을 바라보는 전사들의 눈동자에 경악과 두려움의 빛이 스쳐 지나갔다.
 52|
 53|‘진태경.’
 54|
 55|‘놈에 관한 소문이 전부 사실이었어.’
 56|
 57|‘그토록 많은 추격대를 뿌리치고 이곳까지 오다니. 도대체 어느 정도의 괴물인 거지?’
 58|
 59|당연하게도 이 자리에 있는 전사 중 대다수는 진태경을 직접 마주한 적이 없다.
 60|
 61|아니, 그의 진면목을 확인한 적이 없다고 말해야 옳았다.
 62|
 63|그들에게 있어 지금까지의 진태경은 그저 중원에서 온 이방인이었고 남만인들과는 조금 다른, 희한한 생김새를 지닌 젊은 청년에 불과했다.
 64|
 65|그러나 이제는, 그와 싸워야 한다.
 66|
 67|애뇌산을 물 샐 틈 없이 포위한 채 언제 저곳을 뛰쳐나올지 모를 진태경을 척살하는 것이 자신들에게 내려진 임무였다.
 68|
 69|하지만…….
 70|
 71|‘놈을 막을 수 있을까. 그 괴물을?’
 72|
 73|모두의 뇌리에 떠오른 한 가지 의문.
 74|
 75|남만야수궁의 시작과 역사를 같이한 금지(禁地). 애뇌산에 관한 이야기를 사는 내내 지긋지긋하게 들었던 그들이다.
 76|
 77|그리고 그럴 때마다 늘 빠지지 않는 세 글자가 있었다.
 78|
 79|열화문(烈火門).
 80|
 81|머나먼 중원 땅 어딘가에 존재한다는 미지의 문파.
 82|
 83|아득한 과거, 이 땅에 발을 디딘 열화문의 문주는 남만야수궁이 탄생한 이후에도 백여 년간 계속되던 오독문과의 대전쟁에 종지부를 찍었다고 했다.
 84|
 85|수많은 목숨을 앗아 간 오독문의 극독(劇毒)도, 놈들이 부리던 독물도 그가 불러낸 화염 앞에 촛농처럼 녹아내렸다.
 86|
 87|심지어는 남만야수궁의 최정예 전사 일백을 한 줌 독수로 만들었다는 오독문의 당대 문주조차 그의 힘을 감당하지 못하고 무릎을 꿇었다고 했다.
 88|
 89|‘아니, 산 채로 타 죽었다고 했지.’
 90|
 91|그런데 모두가 어린 시절 재미있게 들었던 옛 전설이, 지금 이 순간 과거를 넘어 현재로 다가왔다.
 92|
 93|바로 자신들의 눈앞에.
 94|
 95|꿀꺽.
 96|
 97|누군가의 마른 침 삼키는 소리가 유난히도 크게 울려 퍼진다. 느슨하게 고삐를 말아쥐고 있던 손에는 어느새 한껏 힘이 들어갔고, 불안하게 흔들리는 눈동자와 함께 동요가 퍼져 나간다.
 98|
 99|그리고 바로 다음 순간이었다. 굳게 닫혀 있던 호위장의 입술이 열린 것은.
100|
101|“무엇이 그리 두렵더냐.”
102|
103|“……!”
104|
105|공력이 실린 목소리가 전사들의 귓가를 파고든다. 호위장은 힘주어 말을 이었다.
106|
107|“놈은 혼자. 우리는 삼천이다.”
108|
109|자신도 모르게 움츠려졌던 전사들의 어깨가 조금씩 펴진다. 흔들리던 시선이 하나둘씩 중심을 되찾기 시작했다.
110|
111|‘그래. 놈이 아무리 강하다 한들, 결국 피륙으로 이루어진 인간.’
112|
113|‘지금껏 들었던 진태경에 관한 소문이 모두 사실이라 해도, 이 군세를 당해 낼 수는 없어.’
114|
115|삼천.
116|
117|무려 삼천이었다. 단 한 사람을 척살하기 위한 숫자로는 차고 넘치다 못해, 터무니없는 머릿수다.
118|
119|엄청난 무위로 오독문을 박살 냈다는 열화문의 문주?
120|
121|자신들이 듣고 자란 이야기를 떠올리면 두려운 마음이 드는 것은 사실이지만, 결국 전설은 전설일 뿐이다.
122|
123|아니, 설령 그가 살아온다 해도 삼천에 달하는 남만의 전사와 맹수들을 단신으로 상대하는 것은 불가능하다. 불가능해야 했다.
124|
125|“잊었느냐. 진태경은 남만을 위험에 빠트린 역도요, 정마대전의 은혜를 잊은 금수만도 못한 한족이다.”
126|
127|빠르게 가까워지는 거대한 화마만큼, 호위장의 목소리에도 힘이 실린다.
128|
129|스릉.
130|
131|“남만의 전사들이여! 자랑스러운 내 형제들이여!”
132|
133|허리춤에서 뽑혀 나온 검이 날카로운 예기를 뿜어낸다.
134|
135|머리 위에서 쏟아진 달빛과 일렁이는 횃불이 새하얀 검신에 부딪쳐 산산이 부서졌다.
136|
137|“놈을 추살하라!”
138|
139|“와아아아아!”
140|
141|차차차창!
142|
143|동시에 뽑혀 나온 수백, 수천의 병장기와 거세게 타오르는 횃불. 그리고 삼천에 달하는 군세가 아득한 함성을 내지르며 애뇌산을 향해 박차를 가하던 바로 그 순간.
144|
145|콰아아아!
146|
147|호위장은, 이 자리의 모든 인간과 맹수는 볼 수 있었다.
148|
149|시뻘건 화마(火魔)를 관통하며 솟구치는 빛의 기둥과 뜨거운 불길 앞에 그림자를 드리운 검은 동산을.
150|
151|아니, 그건 동산이 아니었다.
152|
153|드드드드득!
154|
155|“저게 무슨……!”
156|
157|빠르게 다가오는 검은 동산과 함께 흔들리는 세상 속, 눈을 부릅뜬 채 그 광경을 바라보던 호위장은 알지 못했다.
158|
159|더 이상 바람이 느껴지지 않는다는 것을.
160|
161|쉼 없이 애뇌산을 향해 달려가던 삼천 마리의 맹수가, 약속이라도 한 것처럼 제 자리에 멈춰 섰다는 것을.
162|
163|크르릉.
164|
165|호위장과 평생을 함께한 호랑이가 낮은 울음소리와 함께 고개를 숙인다.
166|
167|아니, 비단 그뿐만이 아니었다.
168|
169|표범도, 곰도, 늑대도. 크고 작은 모든 맹수가 그러했다.
170|
171|스륵.
172|
173|꼬리를 말고, 거대한 몸뚱어리를 눕힌다.
174|
175|그것은 탄생과 동시에 각인되어 있던 본능이자 긴 세월을 거슬러 돌아온 왕에 대한 경배였고, 거부할 수 없는 명령이었다.
176|
177|- 크아아아앙!
178|
179|세상을 집어삼키는 포효와 함께, 청백색의 안광(眼光)이 어둠 속에서 빛났다.
180|
181|
182|
183|* * *
184|
185|
186|
187|저벅. 저벅.
188|
189|나직한 발걸음 소리가 적막한 복도를 울린다.
190|
191|한 사람, 한 사람이 절정에 이른 호위 전사들의 날카로운 눈빛에 시비와 하인들은 엎드려 부복했고, 떨리는 외침이 뒤를 이었다.
192|
193|“구, 궁주를 뵙습니다!”
194|
195|두려움이 묻어 나오는 그들의 외침은, 오직 한 사람을 향한 것이다.
196|
197|철통같은 호위에 둘러싸인 채 내궁(內宮)의 복도를 가로지르던 백상의 시선이 문득 그들을 훑었다.
198|
199|내궁에서 일하는 이들은 부족도, 나이도 다양하다.
200|
201|아직 젖살도 빠지지 않은 어린아이부터, 중년의 사내와 여인. 그리고…… 온통 머리가 하얗게 센 호호백발 노파까지.
202|
203|워낙 늙어 행동거지가 굼뜬 탓에, 홀로 복도의 중앙에서 쩔쩔매는 노파의 모습을 본 호위들이 미간을 찌푸렸다.
204|
205|그들이 충심을 다해 모시는 백상은 남만야수궁의 주인이요, 이 땅의 왕이다. 아니, 왕이어야 한다.
206|
207|죽을 날만 기다리는 늙은이가 앞길을 가로막아서는 안 된다.
208|
209|저벅.
210|
211|그리고 약속이라도 한 듯, 두어 명의 호위가 노파를 향해 걸음을 내디딘 그 순간이었다.
212|
213|“멈추어라.”
214|
215|나직한 목소리와 함께 호위들의 움직임이 덜컥 멈춘다. 자신의 시선에 닿은 노파를 향해, 백상은 들리지 않을 인사를 건넸다.
216|
217|‘오랜만이구려.’
218|
219|긴 세월이 흘렀음에도 낯익은 얼굴이다.
220|
221|백상은 자신의 어린 시절, 야율척과 함께 내궁 안을 들쑤실 때마다 한숨을 푹푹 내쉬던 어느 젊은 여인을 떠올렸다.
222|
223|‘많이 늙었군.’
224|
225|당연한 일이다. 초절정에 이르는 무위로 노화를 늦춘 그와는 달리, 그녀는 시간의 순리(順理)를 고스란히 받아들였을 테니까.
226|
227|“죄, 죄송합니다. 궁주님. 쇤네가 몸이 성치 않은 탓에…….”
228|
229|감히 고개도 들지 못하고 굽실거리는 노파의 모습에, 백상은 문득 의문이 들었다.
230|
231|자신은 왜 수하들을 만류한 것일까.
232|
233|저 노파가 그의 옛 모습을 기억하는 몇 안 되는 사람이어서?
234|
235|그것이 아니라면…….
236|
237|지금 이 순간에도 시시각각 다가오고 있을 ‘그 순간’을 늦추고 싶다는 마음 때문에?
238|
239|‘모를 일이군. 모를 일이야.’
240|
241|씁쓸했다. 여기까지 왔음에도 마음 한구석에 후회가 남아 있다는 것이.
242|
243|그리고 거리낌 없이 자신을 구박하던 그녀가, 이제는 두려움으로 눈조차 마주치지 못한다는 것이 그랬다.
244|
245|‘그리고 이것이, 지금껏 내가 걸어온 길이겠지.’
246|
247|전부 허망한 감상에 불과하다.
248|
249|하나뿐인 의형(義兄)과 함께 전장에서 등을 맞대며 싸우고, 적들의 시체를 깔고 앉아 과실주를 나누어 마시고, 어스름한 달빛 아래에서 만나는 두 남녀를 몰래 지켜보던 날들은 이미 오래전에 지났으니까.
250|
251|“……주군?”
252|
253|조심스러운 호위의 부름에, 백상의 눈동자가 평소처럼 차갑게 가라앉았다.
254|
255|“길을 터라.”
256|
257|“존명.”
258|
259|기다렸다는 듯이 앞으로 나선 호위들이 거칠게 노파를 밀어 낸다.
260|
261|겁에 질린 눈빛으로 더욱 바짝 엎드린 사람들을 굽어보던 백상이 말을 이었다.
262|
263|“또한. 지금 이 시간 부로 내궁에 머무르는 궁인(宮人)들을 추방한다.”
264|
265|“소, 송구합니다만, 궁인들 전부를 말씀이십니까?”
266|
267|“그래. 전부.”
268|
269|궁인은 말 그대로 궁에 머무르며 온갖 잡일을 하는 이들이다. 매 끼니 식사를 준비하는 숙수부터 청소와 빨래를 하는 이까지 전부 궁인이었다.
270|
271|가혹한 추방령은 둘째치고, 크고 작은 부분을 담당하던 그들이 없어진다면 당장 내궁이 제대로 돌아가지 않을 터.
272|
273|도대체 왜, 라는 의문이 목구멍까지 솟구쳤지만 호위 중 누구도 입 밖에 내지 않았다.
274|
275|백상의 말은 곧 법이니까.

That old legend, so entertaining when they were children, had stepped out of the past and into the present.

[P42]
Right before their eyes.

[P43]
Gulp.

[P44]
Someone swallowed, the sound strangely loud. Hands tightened around reins that had been held loosely moments before. Anxious glances spread through the ranks.

[P45]
Then the Captain of the Guards spoke.

[P46]
“What are you so afraid of?”

[P47]
“…!”

[P48]
His voice, carrying internal energy, reached every warrior. He went on, firm and clear.

[P49]
“He is one man. We are three thousand.”

[P50]
Shoulders that had hunched without their owners noticing began to straighten. One by one, the warriors steadied their gazes.

[P51]
*That’s right. No matter how strong he is, he’s made of flesh and blood.*

[P52]
*Even if every rumor is true, he can’t stand against all of us.*

[P53]
Three thousand.

[P54]
For the killing of one man, it was an absurd number.

[P55]
The Fire Gate Clan’s Sect Leader had supposedly destroyed the Five Poisons Sect through sheer martial prowess. The stories they had grown up with still frightened them, but a legend was a legend.

[P56]
Even if that Sect Leader returned from the dead, he could not face three thousand Nanman warriors and beasts alone.

[P57]
He couldn’t.

[P58]
“Have you forgotten? Jin Taekyung is a traitor who put Nanman in danger. He’s a Han Chinese man worse than a beast, one who has forgotten the debt of the Great Faction War.”

[P59]
As the inferno drew closer, the Captain’s voice grew stronger.

[P60]
Shing.

[P61]
“Warriors of Nanman! My proud brothers!”

[P62]
He drew his sword. Its edge gleamed as moonlight and wavering torchlight broke across the white blade.

[P63]
“Hunt him down!”

[P64]
“Waaaaaah!”

[P65]
Clang! Clang! Clang!

[P66]
Hundreds, then thousands of weapons came free. Torches flared, and the army urged its mounts toward Ailao Mountain with a roar.

[P67]
At that instant—

[P68]
Whoosh!

[P69]
The Captain of the Guards saw it. Every human and beast there saw it.

[P70]
A pillar of light rose through the blood-red flames. Against the fire stood the silhouette of a black hill.

[P71]
No. It wasn’t a hill.

[P72]
Rrrrrumble!

[P73]
“What is that…?”

[P74]
The world shook as the dark shape drew nearer. The Captain stared, eyes wide.

[P75]
He did not notice that he could no longer feel the wind.

[P76]
Nor did he notice that the three thousand beasts racing toward Ailao Mountain had stopped as one.

[P77]
Grrrr.

[P78]
The tiger that had spent its life at his side gave a low growl and bowed its head.

[P79]
It was not alone.

[P80]
Leopards, bears, wolves—every beast, large and small, did the same.

[P81]
Rustle.

[P82]
They tucked their tails and lowered their bodies to the ground.

[P83]
It was an instinct etched into them at birth: reverence for a king returned after long ages, and a command they could not resist.

[P84]
—Kraaaaaar!

[P85]
A roar seemed to swallow the world. Blue-white eyes shone in the dark.

[P86]
* * *

[P87]
Step. Step.

[P88]
Quiet footsteps echoed down the silent corridor.

[P89]
The guards’ sharp gazes swept over the maids and servants. Every guard had reached the Peak, and the servants dropped facedown as trembling cries followed.

[P90]
“W-we pay our respects to the Palace Lord!”

[P91]
Their fear was meant for one man.

[P92]
Surrounded by guards, Baeksang walked through the Inner Palace and glanced at the people prostrate before him.

[P93]
They came from different tribes and were of every age: children still round-cheeked with baby fat, middle-aged men and women, and an old woman whose hair had gone entirely white.

[P94]
She moved so slowly that she was still struggling in the middle of the corridor. The guards frowned.

[P95]
Baeksang was the master of the Nanman Beast Palace, the king of this land. Or rather, he had to be. An old woman with little life left could not stand in his way.

[P96]
Step.

[P97]
Two guards moved toward her as though they had agreed on it.

[P98]
“Stop.”

[P99]
They froze at Baeksang’s quiet command. He looked at the old woman and greeted her without speaking.

[P100]
*It’s been a long time.*

[P101]
He knew her face despite the years. When he and Yayul Cheok had run wild through the Inner Palace as boys, she had been a young woman who sighed whenever she saw them coming.

[P102]
*You’ve grown old.*

[P103]
Of course she had. His martial prowess at the Supreme Peak had slowed his aging. She had lived under the ordinary passage of time.

[P104]
“I-I’m sorry, Palace Lord. I’m not as strong as I used to be….”

[P105]
She bowed and groveled, unable even to raise her head. Baeksang found himself wondering why he had stopped his guards.

[P106]
Because she was one of the few who remembered him as he had been?

[P107]
Or because he wanted to delay *that moment*, drawing closer even now?

[P108]
*I don’t know. I truly don’t.*

[P109]
It left a bitter taste. After coming this far, he still had regrets. And the woman who had once scolded him without a second thought was now too afraid to meet his eyes.

[P110]
*This is the path I chose.*

[P111]
Empty sentiment. Nothing more.

[P112]
The days of fighting back-to-back with his only sworn elder brother were long gone. So were the days when they had sat on their enemies’ corpses and shared fruit wine, or secretly watched a man and woman meet beneath the dim moonlight.

[P113]
“…My lord?”

[P114]
At a guard’s cautious call, Baeksang’s eyes settled into their usual coldness.

[P115]
“Clear the way.”

[P116]
“Yes, my lord.”

[P117]
The guards stepped forward at once and shoved the old woman aside.

[P118]
Baeksang looked down at the others, who pressed themselves even lower to the floor in fear.

[P119]
“And as of this moment, expel every palace attendant living in the Inner Palace.”

[P120]
“I-I beg your pardon, my lord. Every attendant?”

[P121]
“Yes. Every one.”

[P122]
The palace attendants lived there and did the work that kept the Inner Palace running. They cooked every meal, cleaned, washed clothes, and handled countless other tasks. Without them, the place would soon cease to function properly.

[P123]
The guards wanted to ask why. None dared.

[P124]
Baeksang’s word was law.

[P125]
He was Nanman’s only Great Chieftain and the only Palace Lord to have received an oath of absolute loyalty from every tribal chieftain. The five tribes that had left the Outer Palace rather than accept him had been stripped of all authority. Even the Miao leadership was locked in the underground prison.

[P126]
There was nothing Baeksang could not command.

[P127]
“…Yes, my lord.”

[P128]
The guards obeyed. Baeksang watched as they led the old woman away, then the other attendants behind her, their faces drained of color.

[P129]
*Perhaps leaving will be a mercy to you.*

[P130]
Soon everything would begin—and end.

[P131]
Even Baeksang did not know how much blood would flow before it was over.

[P132]
*No. I can guess. I just don’t want to believe it.*

[P133]
Perhaps that was why the past month had shaken him more than any other, though he had lived like a man of iron for more than forty years in pursuit of a single goal.

[P134]
*A change of heart. Useless in the end.*

[P135]
Yayul Cheok. Jin Taekyung.

[P136]
Their names crossed his mind as he resumed walking.

[P137]
Step. Step.

[P138]
With every step came another thought.

[P139]
What had become of those two since they disappeared? Where were they now? Did the Southern Heaven Demon Empress know what he had done without anyone else finding out—his final change of heart?

[P140]
*Too late. No one can undo it now.*

[P141]
Baeksang stopped. Only one door remained before him.

[P142]
Beyond it lay the highest dais in the Inner Palace. Below it would be the ten thousand warriors gathered in response to the general mobilization order.

[P143]
*Noon. Tomorrow at noon. Gather every warrior in the palace.*

[P144]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s message from the previous night was clear. The grand plan was already complete.

[P145]
Baeksang spoke suddenly.

[P146]
“The sun is hot.”

[P147]
“…My lord?”

[P148]
The door was still shut, yet he could feel a heat that seemed ready to burn him.

[P149]
What he was about to do was a terrible sin. It could not be forgiven, and it should not be.

[P150]
But…

[P151]
*There’s no other way now, Hwi.*

[P152]
Thinking of the son he missed, Baeksang threw open the door.

[P153]
The sky opened before him. Below stood the assembled warriors. But his gaze—every one of his senses—was fixed elsewhere.

[P154]
Beyond the heads of ten thousand warriors, beyond the wall around the Inner Palace and the fortifications of the Outer Palace, lay a green hill.

[P155]
*That’s…*

[P156]
It was far away, but Baeksang could see a massive White Tiger standing atop it. Its silver mane shone in the noon sun, and someone sat on its back.

[P157]
“…You came. After all.”

[P158]
Behind the White Tiger, beasts began to appear.

[P159]
Thousands of them. Tens of thousands.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P107]
Or because he wanted to delay *that moment*, drawing closer even now?

[P108]
*I don’t know. I truly don’t.*

[P109]
It left a bitter taste. After coming this far, he still had regrets. And the woman who had once scolded him without a second thought was now too afraid to meet his eyes.

[P110]
*This is the path I chose.*

[P111]
Empty sentiment. Nothing more.

[P112]
The days of fighting back-to-back with his only sworn elder brother were long gone. So were the days when they had sat on their enemies’ corpses and shared fruit wine, or secretly watched a man and woman meet beneath the dim moonlight.

[P113]
“…My lord?”

[P114]
At a guard’s cautious call, Baeksang’s eyes settled into their usual coldness.

[P115]
“Clear the way.”

[P116]
“Yes, my lord.”

[P117]
The guards stepped forward at once and shoved the old woman aside.

[P118]
Baeksang looked down at the others, who pressed themselves even lower to the floor in fear.

[P119]
“And as of this moment, expel every palace attendant living in the Inner Palace.”

[P120]
“I-I beg your pardon, my lord. Every attendant?”

[P121]
“Yes. Every one.”

[P122]
The palace attendants lived there and did the work that kept the Inner Palace running. They cooked every meal, cleaned, washed clothes, and handled countless other tasks. Without them, the place would soon cease to function properly.

[P123]
The guards wanted to ask why. None dared.

[P124]
Baeksang’s word was law.

[P125]
He was Nanman’s only Great Chieftain and the only Palace Lord to have received an oath of absolute loyalty from every tribal chieftain. The five tribes that had left the Outer Palace rather than accept him had been stripped of all authority. Even the Miao leadership was locked in the underground prison.

[P126]
There was nothing Baeksang could not command.

[P127]
“…Yes, my lord.”

[P128]
The guards obeyed. Baeksang watched as they led the old woman away, then the other attendants behind her, their faces drained of color.

[P129]
*Perhaps leaving will be a mercy to you.*

[P130]
Soon everything would begin—and end.

[P131]
Even Baeksang did not know how much blood would flow before it was over.

[P132]
*No. I can guess. I just don’t want to believe it.*

[P133]
Perhaps that was why the past month had shaken him more than any other, though he had lived like a man of iron for more than forty years in pursuit of a single goal.

[P134]
*A change of heart. Useless in the end.*

[P135]
Yayul Cheok. Jin Taekyung.

[P136]
Their names crossed his mind as he resumed walking.

[P137]
Step. Step.

[P138]
With every step came another thought.

[P139]
What had become of those two since they disappeared? Where were they now? Did the Southern Heaven Demon Empress know what he had done without anyone else finding out—his final change of heart?

[P140]
*Too late. No one can undo it now.*

[P141]
Baeksang stopped. Only one door remained before him.

[P142]
Beyond it lay the highest dais in the Inner Palace. Below it would be the ten thousand warriors gathered in response to the general mobilization order.

[P143]
*Noon. Tomorrow at noon. Gather every warrior in the palace.*

[P144]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s message from the previous night was clear. The grand plan was already complete.

[P145]
Baeksang spoke suddenly.

[P146]
“The sun is hot.”

[P147]
“…My lord?”

[P148]
The door was still shut, yet he could feel a heat that seemed ready to burn him.

[P149]
What he was about to do was a terrible sin. It could not be forgiven, and it should not be.

[P150]
But…

[P151]
*There’s no other way now, Hwi.*

[P152]
Thinking of the son he missed, Baeksang threw open the door.

[P153]
The sky opened before him. Below stood the assembled warriors. But his gaze—every one of his senses—was fixed elsewhere.

[P154]
Beyond the heads of ten thousand warriors, beyond the wall around the Inner Palace and the fortifications of the Outer Palace, lay a green hill.

[P155]
*That’s…*

[P156]
It was far away, but Baeksang could see a massive White Tiger standing atop it. Its silver mane shone in the noon sun, and someone sat on its back.

[P157]
“…You came. After all.”

[P158]

[P159]
Thousands of them. Tens of thousands.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
